ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $6.43 to the rider (RD-2 refund of the unexempted detour mileage) within 30 days per NS-7; no account flag on the driver (RD-6 not triggered).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI journey (base $3.90, distance $26.31 for 18.66 km, time $7.39, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47; total $39.18) [F7], so deviation mileage flows straight into the fare and RD-2's meter branch governs, not the flat-fare branch [RD-2].

RD-1 is engaged: the record shows a measured off-route segment, 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, adding 4.56 km [F3]. No RD-4 excuse is available: there is no LTA incident on the replaced stretch during the window [F14], and the speed-band records on the expressway and Kampong Bahru Road are band 5 (40–49 km/h), which is not the band 1–2 proxy and in any case cannot exempt on its own [F12][F13][RD-4].

On consent, the chat must be read in context [F10]. At 21:35 the driver asked only "Mind if I pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute?" and at 21:36 the rider agreed: "Sure, no problem." [F8][F9]. That is agreement to a brief stop, not to a route change — the rider agreed to something else, so under RD-5 the agreement does not cover the 4.56 km loop the driver then drove (scope_other), and the driver's own statement that "the rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine" confirms he converted a stop-consent into a route change on his own reasoning; a claim appearing only in his statement is not consent anyway [F11][RD-5]. RD-3 does not exempt the segment either: the place was raised by the driver, not named by the rider, no petrol station was actually reached (the rider's complaint and the absence of any stop measurement), and the driver's own statement places the detour as "a small change of route" rather than a stop at a rider-named point, so the segment counts [RD-3]. The total trip figures corroborate the whole of it: 18.7 km actual vs 13.9 km optimal, +4.8 km, +8.3 min [F1][F2], matching the billed excess distance of $6.77 (4.80 km × $1.4100/km) [F4].

Amount: the rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km = $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km [F7][RD-2]. The only off-route segment is F3, and the excess mileage actually billed for it is 4.56 km (6.27 − 1.71) [F3]; the residual difference up to the recorded 4.80 km excess is corridor noise not attributable to any segment and is not refunded [F4][RD-2]. Refund = 4.56 × $1.4100 = $6.4296, rounded to $6.43 [F3][F7][RD-2]. The metered waiting charge of $0.11 is a legitimate RydeTAXI waiting unit and is not refunded [F5][RD-3].

No account flag: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so the "repeated" condition of RD-6 is not met, and the profile facts are not used to decide the case itself [F17][RD-6].

The driver-side no_action position fails: the rider's 'Sure, no problem' (F9) answered a question about a one-minute petrol stop (F8), not a 4.56 km loop; RD-5 does not extend that consent to the driven segment, and RD-3 does not exempt it since the rider named no place and the driver chose the location (F11).

Any reliance on RD-4 congestion fails: the only traffic records are band 5 (40–49 km/h) on the expressway and Kampong Bahru Road (F12, F13), which are not band 1–2 and cannot exempt alone, and no incident was recorded on the replaced stretch (F14).
